question: Which dance style was kept alive by the Devadasis?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Devadasis, a community of dancers in South India**, are credited with originating the popular dance form of Bharatanatyam.
 
• **Devadasis were women who dedicated their lives to temples**, learning classical Indian dances, and performing at temple rituals
 
• They were also known by various local terms, such as Basivi in Karnataka, Matangi in Maharashtra, and Kalavantin in Goa and Damaon.
 
• **Bharatanatyam was originally known as Sadir or Dasi Attam**.
 
• It was the **first traditional Indian dance** to be adapted for theater and performed widely both in India and abroad

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kuchipudi:

 
 
• It basically performed by a group of actors going from village to village, known as Kusselavas, Kuchipudi derives its name from the Andhra.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi in the 17th century formalized and systematized the tradition.
 
• The advent of Vaishnavism, the dance form became a monopoly of the male Brahmins and began to be performed at temples.
 
 
 
• Kathakali:
 
 
• Kathakali in the temples of Kerala, two forms of dance-drama.
 
• The folk drama traditions later became the source of Kathakali, which derived its name from the words ‘Katha’ meaning story and ‘Kali’ meaning drama.
 
• It is closely related to Koodiyattam (Sanskrit drama tradition) and other ancient martial-arts performances also.
 
• It is a wonderful combination of music, dance, and drama.
 
 
 
• **Odissi**
 
 
• **​**Odissi, also referred to as Orissi in old literature,
 
• It is a major ancient Indian classical dance that originated in the temples of Odisha – an eastern coastal state of India
